metadata.title: Verkio — European work suite, EU-resident
metadata.description: Verkio is the work suite for European businesses that care about EU data residency. Mail, document storage, wikis, calendar, and contacts hosted in the EU, encrypted at rest, GDPR-native by default. Even our DNS lookups stay in the EU.
metadata.ogDescription: Premium European work suite for businesses that care about where their data lives.

hero.headline: The work suite without the noise.
hero.body1: Mail, calendar, contacts, files, wikis, and messaging. One suite for the actual work, without the bloat or the noise.
hero.body2: Built on open standards. Hosted in Europe. Yours to leave, anytime.

suite.headline: Everything your team uses, in one place.
suite.subhead: One login, one address book, one bill. Built on open standards so you're never locked in.

mail.name: Mail
mail.description: Personal and shared inboxes. Use it through the web app or any IMAP client. Bring your own domain.

calendar.name: Calendar
calendar.description: Personal and team calendars. Standards-based (CalDAV) so it works with the apps you already use.

contacts.name: Contacts
contacts.description: Personal and shared address books, over CardDAV. Sync everywhere with no lock-in.

documents.name: Document storage
documents.description: Files and folders with sharing, version history, and granular access controls.

wikis.name: Wikis
wikis.description: Structured pages for team knowledge, with full edit history and linking.

messaging.name: Messaging
messaging.description: Channels, DMs, and threads for team conversations. Searchable, in the same suite as your mail.

capabilities.headline: Built for the real work.
capabilities.subhead: The features teams actually need — not a list designed to look long on a slide.

webmail.name: Webmail that gets out of the way.
webmail.description: A fast, keyboard-first web client — threading, search, labels, three-pane layout. Built to read, write, and archive without the bloat. The webmail you wish Gmail still was.

files.name: Files with keys you control.
files.description: Private and shared folders, granular ACLs, password- and expiry-protected share links. Every file is encrypted at rest with its own AES-256-GCM key on EU object storage — no master key sitting in a US bucket.

calendar.name: A calendar that fits the way you already work.
calendar.description: Full CalDAV under the hood, with a web app supporting month, week, and day views, recurring events, iMIP invitations, and free-busy lookup across teams. Sync to Apple Calendar, Thunderbird, or your phone — no proprietary plug-in to install.

contacts.name: Contacts that move with you.
contacts.description: Personal and shared address books over CardDAV. vCard import and export, group support, no proprietary contact format you have to migrate off of later. Your address book is yours.

filters.name: Mail filters without a manual.
filters.description: A visual rule builder that compiles to standard Sieve under the hood. Pre-built templates for the rules you actually want, plus guardrails that stop you from building a forward loop at 2 a.m.

sharedMailbox.name: Shared mailboxes for real teams.
sharedMailbox.description: A team inbox with assignees, status, and internal notes — projected as IMAP keywords, so it still works in every mail client without a proprietary app. Helpdesk workflow without buying a helpdesk product.

messaging.name: Team messaging without the noise.
messaging.description: Channels for ongoing work, DMs for one-on-one threads, search across both. In the same suite as your mail and docs — one login, one search, one place to look. No engagement metrics, no upsells, no 'is anyone available?' theatre.

api.name: A public API and signed webhooks.
api.description: Scoped bearer tokens, HMAC-signed webhook delivery with a dead-letter queue, an OpenAPI spec, and a JMAP passthrough. Wire Verkio into the CRM, CI, or back-office you already have — no screen-scraping.

auditLog.name: Every admin action, on the record.
auditLog.description: A customer-facing audit log with search, before/after values, and seven-year retention by default — matching Swedish bokföringslagen. Stream events to Splunk, Datadog, or any SIEM, or export to CSV or JSONL.

offboarding.name: Offboarding without the cliff edge.
offboarding.description: When someone leaves the org, their inbox stays accessible for thirty days and can forward to a designated owner — so a customer reply on day fourteen still lands somewhere useful. Anti-loop guards built in, audit-logged, cascade-clear if the owner moves on too.

domains.name: Domains and devices configured in minutes.
domains.description: Add a domain, verify DNS, set a catch-all. We generate Thunderbird XML and Apple .mobileconfig profiles, and host-header autoconfig just works. DNS verification supports ten EU providers including Hetzner, OVH, IONOS, deSEC, Scaleway, and Glesys.

migration.name: Bring your inbox with you.
migration.description: Migrate from Gmail, Outlook, or any IMAP provider in one flow — folders, flags, and threads preserved. We pull, you watch the progress bar. No 'export your mbox and pray' weekend project.

principles.headline: Quiet by design.
principles.subhead: Open standards, calm defaults, one address book, full export. Four choices most suites get backwards.

standards.name: Standards-first.
standards.description: IMAP, SMTP, CalDAV, CardDAV from day one. Use Thunderbird, Apple Mail, Outlook, k-9, or DAVx⁵ — we don't lock you into our app.

quiet.name: Quiet.
quiet.description: No AI features scanning your mail. No engagement notifications. No 'you might be interested in' upsell. We don't compete for your attention — we get out of your way.

unified.name: One suite, one address book.
unified.description: Mail, calendar, contacts, docs, wikis — one login, one address book, one bill. Not five products bolted together with single sign-on.

leave.name: Yours to leave.
leave.description: Full export in open formats anytime. GDPR Article 20 made real, not a support-ticket process. No ransom on the way out.

residency.headline: Where your data lives.
residency.subhead: Every layer of the stack — storage, keys, DNS, vendors — sits inside the EU.

infrastructure.name: EU-owned infrastructure
infrastructure.description: Stored, processed, and backed up inside the EU, on infrastructure owned and operated by European companies.

encryption.name: Encrypted at rest
encryption.description: Encryption keys live in an EU-located KMS we operate, included by default — not an upgrade tier.

dns.name: EU-resolving DNS
dns.description: The lookups that point you at our servers stay in Europe, too.

jurisdiction.name: European jurisdiction
jurisdiction.description: EU jurisdiction, GDPR-native by design. Access requests run through European legal channels.

subprocessors.name: European subprocessors
subprocessors.description: Email delivery, payments, support — every vendor in the data path is EU-domiciled. The list is published; changes get 30 days' notice.

comparison.headline: How Verkio compares.
comparison.subhead: Side-by-side with the two suites most teams default to today.

infrastructure.label: EU-owned infrastructure
infrastructure.info: Verkio runs on infrastructure operated by EU-domiciled providers — never AWS, Google Cloud, or Azure, not even their European regions. Google Cloud and Microsoft Azure are US-owned hyperscalers; their EU regions are still operated by US companies.

cloudAct.label: Outside US CLOUD Act
cloudAct.info: The US CLOUD Act compels US-incorporated companies to produce customer data on request, regardless of where it is stored. Google and Microsoft are US corporations and therefore exposed. Verkio is European with no US entity in the data path.

gdpr.label: GDPR-native by design
gdpr.info: GDPR is built into Verkio's data model — data minimisation, lawful-basis tracking, cascading deletion, machine-readable export. Google and Microsoft are GDPR-compliant via their Data Processing Agreements, but their products were designed for a global market and treat GDPR as a configuration layer.

keys.label: Customer keys managed in the EU
keys.info: Verkio's encryption keys live in an EU-located KMS we operate, by default — no upgrade tier. Google Cloud CMEK and Microsoft Double Key Encryption are paid add-ons (E5 for Microsoft), and the underlying key infrastructure often still runs on US clouds.

standards.label: Open standards (IMAP, CalDAV, CardDAV)
standards.info: Verkio supports IMAP, SMTP, CalDAV, and CardDAV as first-class protocols. Any standards-compliant client (Thunderbird, Apple Mail, k-9, DAVx⁵) connects directly. Google and Microsoft technically support them, but with limited features and mandatory app passwords for accounts using 2FA.

dns.label: EU-resolving DNS
dns.info: Authoritative DNS for verkio.eu is hosted on EU-owned providers — never Route 53 (Amazon), Cloud DNS (Google), or Azure DNS. Google and Microsoft typically route DNS for tenant domains globally, so lookups may transit US-operated nameservers.

ai.label: AI bundled into the suite by default
ai.info: Verkio doesn't ship AI features that summarise your mail, scan your calendar, or train on your data. Google and Microsoft increasingly bundle AI (Gemini, Copilot) into their core suites — with opt-out controls that vary by tier and admin policy.

unifiedSearch.label: Unified search across the suite
unifiedSearch.info: Search in Verkio returns results from every part of the suite at once: mail, calendar, contacts, documents, and wikis appear in the same results. Google and Microsoft offer search across some surfaces but coverage is inconsistent — e.g., Outlook search doesn't find OneDrive docs without leaving Outlook.

hosting.question: Where is the data actually hosted?
hosting.answer: Inside the EU, full stop. Primary storage, backups, and all processing happen on EU infrastructure. No replicas leave the bloc.

cloudAct.question: What about the US CLOUD Act?
cloudAct.answer: Verkio is a Swedish company with no US presence, so the CLOUD Act doesn't apply to us. Foreign access requests go through Swedish and EU legal channels.

clients.question: Will it work with Outlook, Apple Mail, Thunderbird?
clients.answer: Yes. Verkio is standards-based — IMAP, SMTP, CalDAV, CardDAV — so any modern client connects directly.

launch.question: When does Verkio launch?
launch.answer: July 2026. Join the waitlist and we'll be in touch when accounts open.

migration.question: Can I migrate from Google Workspace or Microsoft 365?
migration.answer: Yes. Migration tools for mail, calendar, contacts, and documents are part of the launch plan.

pricing.question: How is pricing structured?
pricing.answer: Per-seat monthly or annual billing in EUR, with no per-feature surcharges. Specifics ship with the launch.

subprocessors.question: Do you use any US-based subprocessors?
subprocessors.answer: Our goal is none in the data path. We publish a current subprocessor list at launch and flag any change before it happens.

leaving.question: What happens to my data if I leave?
leaving.answer: Full export in standard formats. No lock-in, no ransom on the way out.

openSource.question: Is Verkio open-source?
openSource.answer: The client side is built on open standards so any compliant tool works. We'll share more on the backend approach closer to launch.

footer.tagline: A European company. Open standards. Yours to leave.

privacy.metaDescription: How Verkio handles personal data on verkio.eu, our pre-launch waitlist site.
privacy.headline: Privacy Policy
privacy.intro: This notice describes how Verkio handles personal data on verkio.eu, our pre-launch marketing and waitlist site. When the product launches, a separate, fuller privacy notice will replace this one to cover the service itself.

sections.heading: Who we are
sections.body:
Verkio is a European company. We act as data controller for the personal data described below.

You can reach us at hello@verkio.eu.

sections.heading: What we collect
sections.body:
Waitlist: your email address, and optionally a company name. That's it.

Functional cookies: a small NEXT_LOCALE cookie that remembers your language choice. It is not used for tracking.

Server logs: brief request records (IP, user agent, URL) to operate the site safely. Retained for a short operational period; not used to profile you.

No analytics, no marketing trackers, no third-party advertising pixels.

sections.heading: Why we collect it
sections.body:
To notify you when Verkio opens, and to operate this site.

Legal basis under the GDPR: legitimate interest (Art. 6(1)(f)) for the waitlist; necessity for the functional cookie; legitimate interest in network security for server logs.

sections.heading: Where it's stored
sections.body: Inside the European Union, on EU-owned infrastructure. No transfers outside the EU.

sections.heading: How long we keep it
sections.body: Waitlist details until the product launches and you choose to become a customer, or earlier if you ask us to delete them. Server logs only for a short operational period.

sections.heading: Sharing
sections.body: We don't sell your data. We don't share it with advertisers. We don't use third-party trackers. Only Verkio staff with a clear need can see it.

sections.heading: Your rights
sections.body:
Under the GDPR you have rights to access, rectify, erase, restrict, object to processing, and port your data. You can also withdraw consent (where consent is the basis) and complain to your local data protection authority.

To exercise any of these, email hello@verkio.eu. We respond within one month.

sections.heading: Updates
sections.body: When this notice changes we'll update the date above. The product launch will issue a fuller notice that supersedes this one.

sections.heading: Contact
sections.body: Questions about this notice or a data-subject request: hello@verkio.eu.

subprocessors.metaDescription: Third-party services Verkio uses to deliver the product. Each has a Data Processing Agreement on file.
subprocessors.headline: Subprocessors
subprocessors.intro: These are the third-party services Verkio uses to deliver the product. Each has a Data Processing Agreement on file. We give 30 days' notice before adding or replacing a subprocessor.

purposes.hetzner: Cloud servers, Storage Box for backups
purposes.mollie: Subscription billing, payment processing, customer portal

subprocessors.customerBody1: Some product features let you connect a third-party service of your choice. Those third parties are not Verkio subprocessors: you remain the controller of that relationship, and the provider operates under whatever agreement you have with them directly. Verkio acts on your instruction (the saved credential) to do the work you've asked us to do.

dns.name: DNS providers
dns.description: Domain auto-setup writes records via your provider's API. You supply an API token (Hetzner DNS, OVH, IONOS, Cloudflare, Route 53, etc.); we publish the records you've asked us to.

idp.name: Identity providers (SSO/SCIM)
idp.description: When single sign-on ships, you bring your own IdP (Okta, Entra ID, Google Workspace, etc.). Authentication and user lifecycle live in your tenant, not ours.

webhooks.name: Webhook endpoints
webhooks.description: The public API pushes events to URLs you choose. Those endpoints are operated by you or by a recipient you've selected.

forwarding.name: External mail forwarding
forwarding.description: If you set up a forwarding rule to an address outside Verkio, the destination mail server handles the forwarded message under your relationship with them.

siem.name: SIEM and log streaming
siem.description: Audit log streaming pushes events to a destination you control — your own collector, Datadog, Splunk, or any compatible endpoint.

subprocessors.customerBody2: Where we offer a choice of default provider, we default to EU-owned options to match our infrastructure posture. US-domiciled providers are also supported, but only after an explicit per-organisation acknowledgment that the provider is US-domiciled and the relationship leaves EU-owned infrastructure. Acknowledgment and credential save are independently audit-logged.
subprocessors.noticeBody: To receive notifications when this list changes, email <email>subprocessors@verkio.eu</email> and ask to be added to the subprocessor change list.

terms.metaDescription: Terms governing your use of verkio.eu, the Verkio pre-launch marketing and waitlist site.
terms.headline: Terms & Conditions
terms.intro: These terms govern your use of verkio.eu, our pre-launch marketing and waitlist site. Separate, fuller terms will accompany the product itself when it launches.

sections.heading: About
sections.body: verkio.eu is operated by Verkio, a European company. Contact: hello@verkio.eu.

sections.heading: Waitlist
sections.body: Providing your email signs you up to hear from us when Verkio opens. You can leave the waitlist at any time by emailing us. We won't use your details for anything other than launch-related contact.

sections.heading: No commitment
sections.body: Joining the waitlist doesn't guarantee access, doesn't lock pricing, and doesn't form a service contract. Indicative launch dates are exactly that — indicative.

sections.heading: Content & trademarks
sections.body: Text, design, and the Verkio name are owned by Verkio. Please don't reproduce or redistribute them without permission.

sections.heading: Disclaimers
sections.body: This site is provided as-is. We do our best to keep information accurate, but pre-launch product details may change.

sections.heading: Governing law
sections.body: These terms are governed by the laws of Sweden. Disputes will be handled in Swedish courts.

sections.heading: Changes to these terms
sections.body: We may update these terms before launch. Material changes will be reflected by the date above. Continued use of the site means you accept the current version.

wiki.name: Internal wikis
wiki.description: Searchable, versioned spaces for runbooks, decisions, and the institutional knowledge your team writes for itself.

messaging.name: Internal messaging
messaging.description: Channels, DMs, and threads for team conversations — searchable, threaded, and built into the same suite as your mail and docs.

webmail.name: Webmail inbox
webmail.description: A fast, keyboard-first web client for Verkio mail — threading, search, and labels without the bloat.

domainAutoSetup.name: Domain auto-setup
domainAutoSetup.description: Add your domain and we configure MX, SPF, DKIM, DMARC, and autoconfig records for you. No manual DNS work.

migration.name: Migration from Google Workspace and Microsoft 365
migration.description: One-click import of mail, calendar, contacts, and Drive or OneDrive files. With status, retries, and a side-by-side switch-over period.

ssoScim.name: SCIM and OIDC sign-on
ssoScim.description: RFC 7644 SCIM endpoints so Okta / Entra ID / any standard IdP can auto-provision and de-provision users via push, instead of waiting for first sign-in. OIDC sign-on as an alternative to SAML for IdPs that prefer it. SAML SSO already shipped — see above.

emailAliases.name: Email aliases and catch-all
emailAliases.description: Unlimited* aliases per user. Catch-all on your domain so you never miss a misspelled address. Pairs with bring-your-own-domain.

schedule.name: Verkio Schedule
schedule.description: Public scheduling links from your calendar. Like Calendly, but EU-resident, no tracking, and built into the suite.

auditLog.name: Audit log
auditLog.description: Who-accessed-what-when, exposed as both a UI and an API. Stream to your SIEM if you need to.

publicApi.name: Public API
publicApi.description: REST API with bearer-token auth and SIEM-friendly audit-log export. Argon2id-hashed keys, per-key rate limits, OpenAPI 3.1 spec — point your codegen tool at /api/v1/openapi.json or browse the interactive reference at /developers.
publicApi.note: Webhooks, mailbox/domain CRUD, JMAP passthrough, and OAuth 2 still to come.

eidasSigning.name: eIDAS document signing
eidasSigning.description: Legally-binding electronic signatures under eIDAS 2.0. Sign PDFs and documents directly from your document storage.

calendarPolls.name: Calendar polls
calendarPolls.description: Find a time that works for everyone without a Doodle link. Propose multiple slots inside the invite, recipients vote, calendar resolves.

sharedMailbox.name: Shared mailboxes
sharedMailbox.description: Team inboxes for shared addresses like support@ and hello@. Multi-user access, full IMAP/SMTP support, every action recorded in the audit log.

sharedMailboxWorkflow.name: Shared mailbox workflow
sharedMailboxWorkflow.description: Team-inbox view for shared mailboxes: assign conversations to teammates, set status (open / pending / closed), and leave internal notes visible only to the team. Same state is exposed as standard IMAP keywords so Apple Mail / Thunderbird / K-9 power users see assignments + status from their existing client. Real-time inbound tracking auto-creates conversations on every new message; auto-reopens closed threads when customers reply.

sendLaterSnooze.name: Send later, snooze, undo send
sendLaterSnooze.description: Schedule a message for tomorrow at 9am. Snooze a thread until Friday. A 30-second grace period to pull back a send.

compliance.name: SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001
compliance.description: Compliance attestations buyers ask for. Rolling commitment with auditor-ready documentation.

realtimeDocs.name: Real-time document collaboration
realtimeDocs.description: Live multi-cursor editing across documents and wikis. Comments, suggestions, version history — built on open formats.

transactionalEmail.name: EU-resident transactional email API
transactionalEmail.description: An HTTP API to send your application's emails through Verkio. The same EU-resident posture as your inbox, extended to your product.

sieveFilters.name: Server-side rules (Sieve)
sieveFilters.description: Server-side mail filters (Sieve, RFC 5228) you build in the dashboard. Move newsletters to a folder, mute noisy lists, route project mail to the right place — applied at delivery, so the rules fire in every mail client. Five pre-built templates to start from; up to 50 rules per mailbox.

ediscovery.name: eDiscovery and legal hold
ediscovery.description: Place users or mailboxes under hold; search and export across the suite for compliance and legal-discovery workflows.

fileStorage.name: Cloud file storage
fileStorage.description: Private + org-shared file storage with folders, public share links, per-file ACL, multi-GB resumable uploads, and 30-day Trash recovery — all encrypted at rest with EU-managed keys.

sharedMailboxAcls.name: Shared-mailbox per-folder access controls
sharedMailboxAcls.description: Grant readers, repliers, or admins per-folder access inside a shared mailbox using RFC 4314 ACL letter sets. Owners and admins can scope an intern to read-only, a senior to label management, or a manager to delete rights — folder by folder or mailbox-wide.

externalForwarding.name: External email forwarding
externalForwarding.description: Forward a copy of every inbound message to an address at another provider — Gmail, Fastmail, your personal inbox. The destination must confirm by clicking a link before forwarding starts; up to 3 forwards per personal mailbox; every change is recorded in the audit log.

calendar.name: Calendar
calendar.description: Shared calendars, invitations, reminders, and free/busy across the suite. Open CalDAV under the hood — connect Apple Calendar, Thunderbird, or DAVx⁵ from day one and keep every event in sync.

contacts.name: Contacts
contacts.description: Personal and team-shared address books, with CardDAV access from any standards-compliant client. Contacts auto-populate from mail and calendar invites — no manual entry, no platform lock-in.

pwaInstall.name: Installable web app (PWA)
pwaInstall.description: Install Verkio to your home screen on phone or desktop. Offline shell for the inbox, push notifications, and a real-app feel — without a native app store in the middle.

gdprPortability.name: GDPR Article 20 portability export
gdprPortability.description: One-click export of your entire workspace in interoperable open formats — mail as standard mbox, calendars as ICS, contacts as vCard, files in their original formats. Bring it to any other provider. No lock-in, ever.

pgpSmime.name: End-to-end encrypted mail (PGP and S/MIME)
pgpSmime.description: OpenPGP and S/MIME in the webmail, with standard headers so encrypted mail Just Works between Verkio mailboxes and any other PGP- or S/MIME-aware client. Keys you control, never escrowed.

notifications.name: Notifications & web push
notifications.description: Bell icon, in-app inbox, and browser push for the moments that matter — new mail, calendar invites, shared mentions, file shares. Per-channel preferences; nothing leaves your control plane.

discountCodes.name: Discount codes
discountCodes.description: Apply a code at signup or mid-subscription. Percent, flat-amount, or free-month comp; per-customer redemption limits; restrict to specific plans or billing periods. Pricing transparency on every invoice.

universalSearch.name: Universal search
universalSearch.description: One input in the top bar searches Email, Calendar, Contacts, Files, Wikis, and Messages. Grouped results, keyboard-first, sharable URLs. Press / from any page to focus; everything in one place.

tier2Encryption.name: Customer-held-key encryption at rest (opt-in)
tier2Encryption.description: Optional per-mailbox upgrade: Verkio configures Stalwart to encrypt every incoming message to YOUR PGP public key before writing to disk. Your private key stays in your mail client (Thunderbird / Apple Mail / K-9 / Outlook+PGP). Verkio physically cannot read those messages at rest. Trades web inbox + search + push previews for the strongest at-rest posture. Free on every plan — no Microsoft/Google-style upsell. Default Verkio-managed-keys posture (every account, every plan) is unchanged.

samlSso.name: SAML / SSO
samlSso.description: Federated sign-in via Okta, Azure AD, Google Workspace, or any SAML 2.0 IdP. Auto-creates Verkio users on first sign-in (JIT provisioning); group/role claims map to org roles and re-evaluate on every sign-in. SP metadata URL exposed in-app for one-click IdP setup. Owner-only configuration.

signInWithVerkio.name: Sign in with Verkio
signInWithVerkio.description: Privacy-respecting alternative to “Sign in with Google / Apple / Microsoft”. A standard OIDC button any third-party site can integrate — your Verkio account becomes your identity for the open web. EU-resident sign-in flow; no cross-site profiling. Per-site granular consent + a connected-apps dashboard where you revoke any third-party with one click. Free for end users; free for developers in v1.

product.metaDescription: The Verkio product: mail, calendar, contacts, files, wikis, and messaging. Plus the capabilities behind each one.

productMail.metaDescription: Standards-based email with team workflows: shared mailboxes, server-side rules, aliases, autoconfig — all on top of IMAP and SMTP.
productMail.headline: Mail that runs the rest of the suite.
productMail.body: Standards-based email with team workflows built in — shared mailboxes, server-side rules, and aliases that don't feel like add-ons. All on top of an IMAP and SMTP server, so any client works.

webmail.headline: The webmail you'd want to use.
webmail.body: Fast, keyboard-first inbox with threading, search, and labels. The three-pane layout you remember — without the AI nudges, engagement metrics, or 'is anyone available?' theatre.
bullets: Keyboard shortcuts you can actually learn — no commands buried five menus deep.
Full-text search across your whole inbox and every folder.
Threading and labels in a calm three-pane layout.
Composer with drag-and-drop attachments and Markdown.
Works offline-first when you install Verkio as a PWA.

shared.headline: Helpdesk workflow, without buying a helpdesk product.
shared.body: Team inboxes for support@, hello@, billing@. Assignment, status, and internal notes — exposed as IMAP keywords so power users in Thunderbird, Apple Mail, or K-9 see the same state as everyone else.
bullets: Assign a conversation to a teammate, with audit-logged ownership.
Set status — open, pending, closed — and watch a customer reply re-open it.
Per-folder access controls (RFC 4314 ACLs): readers, repliers, admins.
Internal notes visible only to the team.
Multi-user IMAP and SMTP — connect any standards-compliant client.
Distribution lists, alias-to-shared routing, retention forwarding.

rules.headline: Filters that fire wherever you read mail.
rules.body: Build Sieve filters in the dashboard — move newsletters to a folder, mute noisy lists, route project mail to the right place. Applied at delivery, not in the client, so they work everywhere.
bullets: Visual rule builder compiling to RFC 5228 Sieve.
Five pre-built templates: newsletter routing, vacation, archive-by-sender, and more.
Up to 50 rules per mailbox, audit-logged.
Forwarding-loop and bad-DNS guards built in — no 3 AM blast radius.

aliases.headline: All the addresses your team needs.
aliases.body: Unlimited aliases per user. Catch-all on your domain. External forwarding to Gmail, Fastmail, your personal inbox — with explicit confirmation. Distribution lists for the team. All audit-logged.
bullets: Unlimited aliases per user (subject to reasonable use).
Catch-all on your domain so misspelled addresses still land.
External forwarding with double opt-in — destinations confirm before mail flows.
Up to 3 forwards per personal mailbox; every change in the audit log.
Distribution lists and retention forwarding for graceful offboarding.

domains.headline: Bring your domain. Any client.
domains.body: Add a domain and we configure MX, SPF, DKIM, DMARC, and autoconfig records for you. Sign in from Apple Mail, Thunderbird, Outlook, K-9 — anything that speaks IMAP or SMTP. Mobile profiles auto-generated.
bullets: Domain auto-setup across ten EU DNS providers — Hetzner, OVH, IONOS, deSEC, Scaleway, Glesys, and more.
Autoconfig via host header for one-click mail-client setup.
Thunderbird XML and Apple .mobileconfig profiles generated for every account.
IMAP4rev1, SMTP, and JMAP — pick your protocol.
Outbound TLS-only, MTA-STS-aware, with ARC signing on forwards.

standards.headline: No proprietary protocol. No vendor lock-in.
standards.body: Verkio Mail is built on the same RFCs your existing tools already speak. Bring your client. Take your mailbox with you when you leave.

productCalendar.metaDescription: Shared calendars over open CalDAV. Recurring events, iMIP invitations, free/busy. Sync to Apple Calendar, Thunderbird, DAVx⁵ from day one.
productCalendar.headline: Plans where they belong — in your suite.
productCalendar.body: Shared calendars, invitations, and free/busy lookup — over open CalDAV. No proprietary plug-in to install. Sync to Apple Calendar, Thunderbird, DAVx⁵, or your phone, and keep every event in lockstep.

shared.headline: Calendars that match how the team actually works.
shared.body: Personal calendars for your own time, shared calendars for the team, and as many as your org needs. Month, week, and day views in the web app — recurring events, all-day events, time-zone awareness, the basics done right.
bullets: Multiple calendars per user — personal, project, on-call rotation, whatever you need.
Shared with named teammates or whole org, with read or write permissions.
Recurring events with all the standard rules — every Tuesday, third Friday of the month, end of every quarter.
All-day events and time-zone-aware events, both honoured across clients.
Web app with month, week, and day views — keyboard shortcuts included.

open.headline: CalDAV under the hood. Your client of choice on top.
open.body: Verkio Calendar speaks CalDAV — the same protocol Apple Calendar, Thunderbird, and DAVx⁵ already know. No proprietary connector to download, no 'works best in our app' sleight of hand. Use the web app, the client you already have, or both.
bullets: Sync to Apple Calendar on macOS and iOS — drop-in setup, no extension.
Sync to Thunderbird via built-in CalDAV — your existing mail client gets your calendar.
Sync to DAVx⁵ on Android — full two-way over a single account.
iCalendar import and export so calendars round-trip cleanly when you move.

invites.headline: iMIP invitations, not screenshots.
invites.body: Send standards-compliant iMIP invitations and your invitees can RSVP from any standard mail or calendar client — Gmail included. Free/busy lookup across your team, so you stop the 'are you free at 2?' thread before it starts.
bullets: iMIP invitations (RFC 6047) that work in Gmail, Outlook, Apple Calendar, and Thunderbird.
RSVP statuses (accepted, tentative, declined) tracked and updated in real time.
Free/busy lookup across teammates — find a slot without screen-sharing your calendar.
Calendar polls on the roadmap (Q2 2027) for when free/busy isn't enough.

standards.headline: RFCs all the way down.
standards.body: Verkio Calendar is built on the same open standards your existing tools already speak. Bring your client. Take your calendar with you when you leave.

productContacts.metaDescription: Personal and team-shared address books over open CardDAV. vCard sync. Auto-populated from mail and calendar invites. No proprietary contact format.
productContacts.headline: An address book that follows you.
productContacts.body: Personal and team-shared address books over open CardDAV. vCard sync to any standards client. Contacts auto-populate from mail and calendar invites — so you don't end up retyping addresses you already know.

shared.headline: Your contacts, your team's contacts, never confused.
shared.body: Personal address books for the people in your life. Shared address books for the team — sales, support, customer accounts. Per-book access so the right people see the right contacts and no more.
bullets: Multiple address books per user — personal, work, project-specific.
Shared address books with named teammates or whole org.
Contact groups for distribution and bulk operations.
vCard import and export so you can bring contacts in and take them out cleanly.

open.headline: CardDAV. Bring any client.
open.body: Verkio Contacts speaks CardDAV — the same protocol Apple Contacts, Thunderbird, and DAVx⁵ already know. Your address book is yours: portable, syncable, never trapped in a proprietary format.
bullets: Sync to Apple Contacts on macOS and iOS over CardDAV — no plug-in.
Sync to Thunderbird and DAVx⁵ on Android.
vCard 4.0 import and export — round-trip preserves photos, custom fields, groups.
No proprietary contact format. Leave with your data intact.

integrated.headline: Contacts that show up before you need them.
integrated.body: Send mail to someone new and their address quietly enters your address book. Accept a calendar invite and the organiser is there too. One identity across mail, calendar, and messaging — no double entry, no duplicate cards.
bullets: Auto-add from sent mail (you can disable per-account).
Auto-add from calendar invites — organisers and attendees both.
Dedup heuristics so the same person doesn't show up three times.
One identity across mail, calendar, and messaging — one card, all surfaces.

standards.headline: Built on the standards your tools already speak.
standards.body: Bring your client. Take your contacts with you when you leave. No proprietary format you'll need to migrate off later.

productFiles.metaDescription: File storage with EU-managed keys, per-file ACLs, share links with expiry, multi-GB resumable uploads, 30-day Trash recovery.
productFiles.headline: Files with keys you control.
productFiles.body: Private and team-shared file storage with per-file access controls, encrypted at rest with EU-managed keys, with resumable multi-GB uploads and a 30-day Trash. No master key sitting in a US bucket.

privateShared.headline: Folders that match the way your team actually works.
privateShared.body: Your private workspace for drafts. Shared folders for the team. Org-wide folders for everyone. Granular ACLs per file or per folder, so you can scope a contractor to one project without exposing the rest of the drive.
bullets: Private folders that only you can see.
Shared folders with named teammates or whole teams.
Org-wide folders for the things everyone needs.
Per-file ACLs — readers, editors, owners.
Audit-logged: every share, every grant, every revoke.

encryption.headline: Per-file keys held in the EU.
encryption.body: Every file gets its own AES-256-GCM data-encryption key. Those keys are wrapped by Vault Transit on an EU-resident key server — not a US KMS, not a hyperscaler. If a disk walks out of the data centre, your files don't go with it.
bullets: Per-file AES-256-GCM encryption — every file, every plan, no upcharge.
Data-encryption keys wrapped by Vault Transit on EU-resident infrastructure.
Storage on Hetzner EU object storage — no US bucket holds your data.
Customer-held-key encryption shipping June 2026 — even Verkio can't read it.

uploads.headline: Multi-GB uploads that survive bad coffee-shop Wi-Fi.
uploads.body: Resumable uploads pick up where you left off when your connection drops. A 30-day Trash catches accidental deletes. Format-preserving: whatever you upload comes back the same bits when you download it.
bullets: Resumable uploads — interrupted at 80%, resume from 80%, not from 0.
Files up to the storage cap on your plan; no per-file size limit.
30-day Trash — recover deleted files without a support ticket.
Format-preserving — your PDF, video, or .docx round-trips unchanged.

sharing.headline: Share links with guardrails.
sharing.body: Send a link to anyone, not just Verkio users. Add a password if it's sensitive. Set an expiry so old links don't haunt you. Every share is in the audit log — who shared what, when, with whom.
bullets: Public share links for downloading without an account.
Password protection per share — share the link, share the password separately.
Expiry date — links self-destruct after a date or a number of views.
Audit-logged so you always know what's been shared with whom.

standards.headline: Open formats, standard cryptography, EU infrastructure.
standards.body: No proprietary file format. No US-hyperscaler key custody. Your files stay yours and round-trip unchanged.

productWikis.metaDescription: Versioned, searchable team knowledge spaces. Personal, team-shared, and org-wide scopes. Built on CommonMark Markdown.
productWikis.headline: The knowledge your team writes for itself.
productWikis.body: Structured, versioned spaces for runbooks, decisions, onboarding, and the institutional knowledge your team would otherwise reinvent every six months. Searchable, linkable, in the same suite as your mail and calendar.

versioned.headline: Every edit recorded.
versioned.body: Wikis aren't just a place to write; they're a place to track how decisions evolved. Every change is captured, attributed, and reversible — useful for compliance, and useful for figuring out who broke the runbook.
bullets: Full edit history per page — see what changed, when, by whom.
Diff view between any two revisions.
Restore an earlier version with one click.
No silent overwrites — concurrent edit detection keeps work safe.

scopes.headline: Personal, team-shared, org-wide.
scopes.body: Some pages are for you — drafts, weekly notes. Some are for your team — runbooks, project pages. Some are for the whole org — onboarding, policies, the kitchen Wi-Fi password. Three clear scopes, no permission spelunking.
bullets: Personal — drafts and notes only you see.
Shared with me — pages your team has shared with you.
Shared with org — pages everyone in the org can read.
Move between scopes with one click; permissions update accordingly.

linked.headline: Pages that find each other.
linked.body: Wikilinks for connecting pages, full-text search for finding them, and hierarchy for browsing them. The knowledge graph builds itself as your team writes.
bullets: Wikilinks — [[Page Title]] resolves anywhere in your wiki.
Full-text search across pages, with content snippets in results.
Hierarchy and breadcrumbs — folders and parent pages for navigation.
Backlinks panel — see every page that links to the one you're on.

standards.headline: CommonMark Markdown. HTML export. Yours to leave.
standards.body: Wiki pages are stored as Markdown — the same format you'd write in any editor, on any platform. Export the whole thing as HTML or download per-page Markdown whenever you want.

productMessaging.metaDescription: Channels, DMs, and threads for team conversations. Same login, same search, same audit log as the rest of your suite.
productMessaging.headline: Quick conversations, same login.
productMessaging.body: Channels for team work, DMs for one-on-ones, threads to keep replies untangled. Searchable next to your mail, calendar, and wiki — not a separate tab to keep up with.

channels.headline: The shapes a real team needs.
channels.body: Channels for ongoing work — #engineering, #support, #social. DMs for one-on-ones. Threads inside both, so a discussion about a thing doesn't clobber the rest of the room.
bullets: Public channels for team-wide work and announcements.
Private channels for sensitive projects, invitation-only.
Direct messages, one-on-one or small groups.
Threaded replies so multiple conversations can happen in one channel.

inSuite.headline: One login. One search. One audit log.
inSuite.body: Messaging shares the same identity as your mail and calendar. Searching for a customer name pulls messages, emails, invites, and wiki pages in one go. The same audit log that records mail actions records messaging actions too.
bullets: Same login as the rest of your Verkio account — no separate Slack tax.
Universal search across messages, mail, calendar, contacts, files, wikis.
Same audit log surface for compliance and operator review.
No second billing line — included in your suite.

noNoise.headline: Built for work, not for engagement.
noNoise.body: No 'someone is typing' anxiety. No streaks. No 'you might be interested in' sidebar. Messaging is a tool — it shows up when you need it and stays out of the way when you don't.
bullets: No engagement metrics — we don't count how often you check the app.
No read receipts that pretend to be a contract.
No status pressure — set yourself as busy without a streak guilt-trip.
Per-channel notifications you actually control, not workarounds for default chaos.

whyVerkio.metaDescription: Why teams choose Verkio: quiet software, open standards, EU residency, no lock-in.

product.headline: Mail, calendar, contacts, files, wikis, and messaging.
product.body: One suite. Built on open standards so you're never locked in.

whyVerkio.headline: Quiet software, EU-resident by default.
whyVerkio.body: Open standards, calm defaults, full export anytime.

whatWeDontHave.headline: Things we deliberately don't have.
whatWeDontHave.subhead: Verkio is defined as much by what we leave out.
items: AI features that quietly read your mail.
Engagement metrics counting how addicted you are.
Read receipts that work differently in every client.
A 'team activity' feed nobody asked for.
Data brokers anywhere in the subprocessor list.

founderNote.body: Hi, I'm Benji. I built Verkio because every time Gmail rolled out a new AI feature my IT-admin friends sighed a little harder. I think email should be boring, yours, and built to last decades — and that the only sustainable way to build that is from inside the EU, on open standards, by a small company that doesn't need to grow forever. If that resonates, join the waitlist.

notFound.headline: You've reached an address that doesn't exist.
notFound.body: Like a Gmail label, basically. Let's get you back home.
